subject: GPU pool rollout scope & milestone plan for Acme Cloud Dedicated
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@acmecloud.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Cloud Infrastructure Team <infra@acmecloud.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated GPU pool — initial requirements attached

Hi Rishi / Marissa,

Thanks for the intro call yesterday. As discussed, we want Redwood Dedicated for low-latency inference for our customer-facing features. Attached is a short requirements spreadsheet with our expected traffic windows and model sizes. Key asks up-front: 

- Primary region: us-west-2; secondary: eu-west-1 for DR.
- Baseline sustained capacity: ~8 x A100-class GPUs for steady inference.
- Burst capacity during promos: ability to temporarily scale to 24 GPUs for ~2 hour windows, 2-3 times/week.
- Prefer autoscaling cooldown of 5 minutes and fast warm-up for KV cache.
- Need canary and rollback plan; procurement needs cost estimate for reserved vs. burst usage.

Also attaching a simple traffic histogram (sheet tab). Can you confirm lead times for regional capacity and a recommended initial node type? We have a renewal decision in 6 weeks and would like a clear rollout plan.

Attachments: acme_gpu_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks,
Samir
Head of Platform
Acme Cloud
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool — initial requirements attached

Samir — thanks for the spreadsheet and the clear asks. High level reply and proposed next steps below: 

Proposed initial configuration (can iterate after traffic validation):
- Region: provision in us-west-2 (primary) with reserved pool sized to 8 GPUs (A100 80GB equiv).
- Burst policy: pre-warmed burst nodes to allow +16 GPUs (total 24) using reserved warmable instances + short-lived burst instances.
- Autoscaling: target CPU/GPU queue-based scaling with 5m cooldown, scale-up aggressive (scale factor 2) and scale-down conservative (factor 1.2) to avoid flapping.
- KV cache: recommend prefix caching for top 50% of requests, warm-up job during deployments.

Schedule suggestion:
1) This week: confirm traffic SLAs and tagging (who owns DR).
2) Week 1 (provisioning): reserve primary pool and stand up test cluster in us-west-2.
3) Week 2 (validation): run synthetic and shadow traffic, tune batching and kernel settings.
4) Week 3 (canary): ramp 10% of real traffic, run smoke tests, rollback window 4 hours.
5) Week 4 (go-live): full cutover once metrics stable for 48 hours.

Action items for Acme: confirm peak window times and whether promos are predictable or ad-hoc; confirm if eu-west DR must be active-passive or active-active.

I'll loop in Jonas to call out any constraints on kernel/quantization selection and capacity lead times. I'll put a draft mutual action plan in Drive and share.

—Rishi
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@acmecloud.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 10:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool — initial requirements attached

Hi all — quick technical notes to factor into the plan: 

- Node type: A100 80GB (or equivalent with 80GB VRAM) is the minimum for the largest model you listed. If you want to get token-level cost down we can also look at 4-bit quantized variants on 80GB A100s or 48GB A6000-class with tensor-splitting.
- Kernel selection: we'll compile kernels based on the actual max sequence length; please confirm typical request sequences (you mentioned 1024 tokens for most API calls).
- KV cache behavior: we should enable sticky routing for sessions that benefit from KV reuse; warm-up can be a small replay of last 24 hours of traffic — that reduces initial latency but costs extra tokens during warm-up.
- EU capacity: current lead time for eu-west-1 A100 80GB reserved capacity is ~3 weeks in our scheduling window. If Acme needs faster DR, we can discuss active-active with smaller footprint in EU.

I attached a short capacity sketch and conservative timeline I use for Dedicated onboarding. If we go to contract this week, we can target provisioning in us-west-2 by Week 1 as Rishi suggested but EU will likely be +2 weeks.

Attachments: redwood_initial_capacity_plan.pdf

—Jonas
Infrastructure Lead, Serving Runtime
From: Samir Patel <samir@acmecloud.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Acme Cloud Infrastructure Team <infra@acmecloud.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool — initial requirements attached

Thanks Rishi and Jonas — that's helpful. A few clarifications and asks: 

- Peak windows are typically 11:00-14:00 PT on promo days (we run ~3 promos/month). Otherwise steady traffic is lower.
- We want a documented canary runbook with exact health-check thresholds and rollback triggers (CPU/GPU latency P95 > 200ms, error rate > 0.5% as examples). Can you propose default thresholds?
- Procurement: need a rough cost delta for Reserved (monthly commit) vs. burst-on-demand for planning. Also please include estimate for pre-warming costs for the KV cache job.
- SLA: we will ask for a 99.9% availability objective and an escalation path/response time for Sev1 incidents during promos.

If you can add these to the mutual action plan and include a simple cost table we can present to finance next week, that would speed decisioning.

Thanks — Samir
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool — initial requirements attached

Samir — looping in the Customer Success and Operations owners and attaching a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that captures the milestones you and Rishi discussed. Summary and next steps below: 

MAP highlights (draft):
- Kickoff & contract signature: target by 2027-06-28.
- Provisioning (us-west-2): Start 2027-06-29, expected ready-for-validation 2027-07-03.
- Validation testing (shadow + synthetic): 2027-07-03 -> 2027-07-09.
- Canary (10% traffic): 2027-07-10 -> 2027-07-11 with rollback window to 07-11 20:00 PT.
- Go-live target: 2027-07-12 pending pass/fail criteria.

Acceptance criteria (examples):
- Performance: P95 inference latency <= 180ms on steady traffic; 95th percentile token cost within 10% of expected.
- Reliability: error rate < 0.2% during validation; <0.5% during promos.
- Operational: automated scaling within configured cooldowns; canary health checks green for 48 hours.

Deliverables we will provide: MAP document, runbook (including canary/rollback thresholds you requested), cost table (Reserved vs burst), weekly standups during rollout, and a DocuSign link for the reserved capacity addendum.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_ACME_v1.docx
DocuSign: https://docusign.com/link/txn-ACME-DED-2027
Drive MAP: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-acme-gpu-requirements

Can you confirm: (1) the promo peak windows above, and (2) whether Acme wants eu-west DR to be active-passive or active-active? Once confirmed we'll lock dates and share the runbook and cost table.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
